Each marker names a clause that only the gate, audit or seal can produce: gate records, the DG7 reviews and audit, the pipeline after approval, verify-seal, the final report, the progress.md gate update, or the auditor's decisions on the D-270 hits and the A27 K11 partial. I accept the Q19 extension as a faithful disclosure for the 18 rows, with one exception. REQ-DLV-012's disclosure undercounts the DG7 C3 hits: it says six, and there are seven. That is F-DG7-960, kept OPEN separately. The mechanism F-DG7-935 is about (SPECIFIED rows blocking validateGate) is repaired.

NOT closed on candidate 60dd90b6. The finding's own expected result is that the release's disclosure of DG7's protocol hits (known limitations, release notes and the REQ-DLV-012 register notes) covers every handback in the frozen candidate. Part of this is repaired. The FE-C3 handback is now disclosed in the register and the release notes. known-limitations.md is regenerated from protocol-audit-r3.json and shows 'C3 handback-sections | REQ-DLV-012 | DG7 | HIT | 7'. known-limitations --check and check-handover pass, and fail when the round-2 file or a hand-edited count is put back. But my own protocol-audit.mjs --all run on this candidate (281 hits, the same as the shipped r3 report) finds SEVEN DG7 C3 hits. The seventh is docs/delivery/handbacks/DG7/T-DG7-DO-D8-devops-engineer.md, a round-2 repair task (exit 1, continued by DO-D8B), which has no merge-instructions section. Its sections are 1. Files changed, 2. Behaviour, 3. Checks run, 4. Known gaps and 5. Open questions. The REQ-DLV-012 register notes (AN-P7F) and the generated release notes still read 'the D-270 C3 hits (six, F-DG7-960 included)'. They name only the five D-270 handbacks plus FE-C3. The DO-D8 hit is named nowhere, and D-270 and D-274 do not cover it. So the handover contradicts itself: known-limitations says 7, the release notes and the register say six. The release-auditor would decide on an undercounted set (REQ-S21-003's later clause: every disclosed deviation listed in the release notes). This is the same defect class as round 2, now with a new handback. Repair: disclose the DO-D8 hit in the REQ-DLV-012 notes and regenerate the release notes, or have the user's D-270/D-274 disclosure decision cover it explicitly. No behavioural effect.
